title: C3NN-SBI: Learning Hierarchies of $N$-Point Statistics from Cosmological Fields with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: Cosmological analyses are moving past the well understood 2-point statistics to extract more information from cosmological fields. A natural step in extending inference pipelines to other summary statistics is to include higher order N-point correlation functions (NPCFs), which are computationally expensive and difficult to model. At the same time it is unclear how many NPCFs one would have to include to reasonably exhaust the cosmological information in the observable fields. An efficient alternative is given by learned and optimized summary statistics, largely driven by overparametrization through neural networks. This, however, largely abandons our physical intuition on the NPCF formalism and information extraction becomes opaque to the practitioner. We design a simulation-based inference pipeline, that not only benefits from the efficiency of machine learned summaries through optimization, but also holds on to the NPCF program. We employ the heavily constrained Cosmological Correlator Convolutional Neural Network (C3NN) which extracts summary statistics that can be directly linked to a given order NPCF. We present an application of our framework to simulated lensing convergence maps and study the information content of our learned summary at various orders in NPCFs for this idealized example. We view our approach as an exciting new avenue for physics-informed simulation-based inference.

AI.tldr: A simulation-based inference framework that combines neural network efficiency with physical interpretability by linking learned summaries to N-point correlation functions (NPCFs) for cosmological analysis.
AI.motivation: Cosmological analyses need to move beyond 2-point statistics to extract more information, but higher-order NPCFs are computationally expensive and difficult to model. While neural networks offer efficient learned summaries, they abandon physical intuition from the NPCF formalism, making information extraction opaque.
AI.method: Develop a simulation-based inference pipeline using Cosmological Correlator Convolutional Neural Network (C3NN), which extracts summary statistics that can be directly linked to given-order NPCFs. The approach maintains the NPCF program while benefiting from machine learning optimization.
AI.result: Applied framework to simulated lensing convergence maps and studied information content of learned summaries at various NPCF orders. Demonstrated the approach as an effective method for physics-informed simulation-based inference.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides an exciting new avenue for physics-informed simulation-based inference that combines the efficiency of machine-learned summaries with the physical interpretability of NPCFs, addressing limitations of both traditional NPCF approaches and black-box neural network methods.

title: The Sign-Switching of the Cosmological Constant
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures. Contribution to the proceedings of the Corfu Summer Institute 2025 "School and Workshops on Elementary Particle Physics and Gravity" (CORFU2025) 2 - 8 September, 2025 Corfu, Greece
summary: We propose and investigate a class of dynamical dark energy models in which the cosmological constant evolves from negative values in the early Universe to a positive value at low redshifts. This framework includes a generalised ladder-step evolution, as well as smooth-transition scenarios, providing a unified description of sign-changing cosmological constants. We analyse the theoretical construction and background dynamics of these models using cosmographic diagnostics. Extending this study to the linear perturbation regime, we solve the perturbation equations from the radiation-dominated era with adiabatic initial conditions. We examine the evolution of the matter density contrast, gravitational potential, and the $fσ_8$ observable. Our results are compared against the standard $Λ$CDM model and confronted with current observational data, illustrating the phenomenological viability of sign-changing dark energy models and revealing distinctive imprints on cosmic structure formation arising from the transition of the cosmological constant.

AI.tldr: Dynamical dark energy models where cosmological constant evolves from negative to positive values, analyzed through background dynamics and linear perturbations, showing phenomenological viability and distinctive structure formation imprints.
AI.motivation: To investigate dynamical dark energy models where the cosmological constant changes sign from negative in early Universe to positive at low redshifts, providing a unified framework for sign-changing cosmological constants beyond standard ΛCDM.
AI.method: Propose class of models with generalized ladder-step evolution and smooth-transition scenarios; analyze theoretical construction and background dynamics using cosmographic diagnostics; extend to linear perturbation regime solving perturbation equations from radiation-dominated era with adiabatic initial conditions.
AI.result: Models show phenomenological viability when compared against ΛCDM and current observational data; reveal distinctive imprints on cosmic structure formation (matter density contrast, gravitational potential, fσ₈ observable) arising from cosmological constant transition.
AI.conclusion: Sign-changing dark energy models provide viable alternatives to ΛCDM with unique signatures in cosmic structure formation due to the transition of cosmological constant from negative to positive values.

title: Testing the cosmic distance-duality relation with localized fast radio bursts: a cosmological model-independent study
summary: We test the Etherington cosmic distance-duality relation (CDDR), by comparing Type Ia supernova (SNIa) luminosity-distance information from the Pantheon+ compilation with an angular-diameter-distance reconstructed from localized Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs). The core of our methodology is a data-driven reconstruction from FRBs using artificial neural networks (ANNs): we infer a smooth mean extragalactic dispersion-measure relation and use its redshift derivative to recover $H(z)$ and hence $D_\mathrm{A}^{\rm FRB}(z)$ without assuming a parametric form for the expansion history. Possible deviations from CDDR are parameterized through three one-parameter models of $η(z)\equiv D_\mathrm{L}/[(1+z)^2D_\mathrm{A}]$. We implement two complementary likelihoods: (i) a direct approach using individual SNIa with the full Pantheon+ covariance, and (ii) a machine-learning approach in which we reconstruct the SN Hubble diagram on the FRB redshift grid, propagating SN and FRB uncertainties into non-diagonal covariance matrices via Monte Carlo and bootstrap realizations. Within the FRB reconstruction, we anchor the mean extragalactic dispersion measure at $z=0$, which yields a data-driven constraint on the average host/near-source contribution $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host}=128.8\pm 34.1\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ ($3σ$ of statistical confidence). We find that both likelihood implementations give consistent posteriors and no statistically significant evidence for departures from CDDR at the current precision.

AI.tldr: Testing cosmic distance-duality relation using SNIa luminosity distances and FRB angular-diameter distances with neural network reconstruction, finding no significant deviations from CDDR.
AI.motivation: To test the Etherington cosmic distance-duality relation (CDDR) which relates luminosity distance and angular diameter distance, using independent distance measurements from different astrophysical probes to search for potential violations of this fundamental cosmological relation.
AI.method: Combines Type Ia supernova luminosity distances from Pantheon+ with angular-diameter distances reconstructed from Fast Radio Bursts using artificial neural networks. FRB dispersion measures are used to infer smooth extragalactic dispersion-measure relation, then derive H(z) and D_A(z) without parametric expansion assumptions. Two likelihood approaches: direct SNIa comparison with full covariance, and ML reconstruction of SN Hubble diagram on FRB grid with Monte Carlo/bootstrap uncertainty propagation.
AI.result: No statistically significant evidence for departures from CDDR at current precision. Both likelihood implementations yield consistent posteriors. Also derived data-driven constraint on average host/near-source dispersion measure: DM_host = 128.8 ± 34.1 pc cm⁻³ (3σ confidence).
AI.conclusion: The cosmic distance-duality relation holds within current observational precision when tested with SNIa and FRB distance measurements. The neural network reconstruction of FRB dispersion measures provides a viable data-driven approach for cosmological tests without parametric assumptions about expansion history.

title: A Sample of Nearby Isolated Dwarf Galaxies: A First Look at the Mass Function of Field Dwarfs
comment: Submitted to ApJ and posted after responding to referee report. Comments welcome
summary: We present the results of the Exploration of Local VolumE Survey - Field (ELVES-Field), a survey of the dwarf galaxies in the Local Volume (LV; $D<10$ Mpc) over roughly $3,000$ square degrees, focusing on the field dwarf population. Candidates are detected using a semi-automated algorithm tailored for low surface brightness dwarfs. Using tests with injected galaxies, we show the detection is $50\%$ complete to $m_g\sim20$ mag and $M_\star \sim 10^6$ $M_\odot$. Candidates are confirmed to be true nearby dwarfs through distance measurements including redshift, tip of the red giant branch, and surface brightness fluctuations. We identify isolated, field dwarfs using various environmental criteria. Over the survey footprint, we detect and confirm 95 LV dwarfs, 44 of which we consider isolated. Using this sample, we infer the field dwarf mass function and find good agreement at the high-mass end with previous redshift surveys and with the predictions of the IllustrisTNG simulation. This sample of isolated, field dwarfs represents a powerful dataset to investigate aspects of small-scale structure and the effect of environment on dwarf galaxy evolution.

AI.tldr: ELVES-Field survey identifies 95 Local Volume dwarf galaxies (44 isolated) using semi-automated detection, confirming distances via multiple methods to study field dwarf population and mass function.
AI.motivation: To systematically study the field dwarf galaxy population in the Local Volume (D<10 Mpc) over a large area (~3000 sq deg), focusing on isolated dwarfs to understand small-scale structure and environmental effects on dwarf galaxy evolution.
AI.method: Semi-automated algorithm tailored for low surface brightness dwarf detection; completeness testing with injected galaxies; distance confirmation via redshift, tip of the red giant branch (TRGB), and surface brightness fluctuations (SBF); environmental criteria to identify isolated field dwarfs.
AI.result: Detected and confirmed 95 Local Volume dwarfs, 44 classified as isolated; 50% completeness to m_g~20 mag and M_*~10^6 M_⊙; field dwarf mass function shows good agreement at high-mass end with previous redshift surveys and IllustrisTNG simulations.
AI.conclusion: The ELVES-Field survey provides a powerful dataset of isolated field dwarfs for investigating small-scale structure and environmental effects on dwarf galaxy evolution, with mass function consistent with simulations and previous surveys.

title: Inflationary Reheating to Preheating - A Personal Account
summary: This is a personal account of the early work that led to what is now known as the ``preheating stage" of inflationary cosmology. The broader applicability of the underlying instability mechanisms in cosmology are indicated.

AI.tldr: Personal account of early work on inflationary preheating mechanisms and their cosmological applications
AI.motivation: To document the historical development of preheating theory in inflationary cosmology and highlight the broader relevance of the underlying instability mechanisms
AI.method: Historical narrative and conceptual analysis of early theoretical work on parametric resonance and instability mechanisms in inflationary models
AI.result: Established foundation for what became known as the "preheating stage" of inflation, identifying key instability mechanisms with wide cosmological applicability
AI.conclusion: The early work laid groundwork for understanding post-inflationary reheating processes, with identified instability mechanisms proving relevant beyond specific inflationary contexts

title: The Epoch of Reionization 21 cm Bispectrum at $z=8.2$ from MWA data II: Smooth Component Filtering
summary: The 21 cm bispectrum (BS) offers a powerful probe of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), but its observational access is severely hindered by dominant astrophysical foregrounds. Considering Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) observations at $154.2~\mathrm{MHz}$ ($z=8.2$), we mitigate the foregrounds with Smooth Component Filtering (SCF) and estimate the 21 cm BS. We validate the pipeline using a simulated 21 cm signal and show that the input BS is recovered for modes $k_{\parallel} \ge [k_\parallel]_f=0.135~{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. Applied to actual data, the SCF produces substantial foreground suppression, reducing the amplitude of the cylindrical BS $B(k_{1\perp},k_{2\perp},k_{3\perp},k_{1\parallel},k_{2\parallel})$ by $3-4$ orders of magnitude. The artifacts due to the missing frequency channels in the data are also suppressed. The resulting EoR window is significantly cleaner at small $k_{\perp}$. We adopt the region $(k_{1 \perp},k_{2 \perp},k_{3 \perp})\leq 0.026~{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and $(k_{1\parallel},k_{2\parallel},k_{3\parallel})>0.135~{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ to evaluate the 3D spherical BS and constrain the EoR signal. By combining estimates over all triangle shapes, we place the lower and upper limits on the mean cube brightness temperature fluctuations $Δ^3$. The estimates are consistent with statistical fluctuations from system noise. The most stringent lower limit $Δ^3_{\rm LL}=-(1.25\times 10^4)^3~{\rm mK}^3$ and upper limit $Δ^3_{\rm UL}=(1.22\times 10^4)^3~{\rm mK}^3$ are obtained at $k_1=0.281~{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. Additional observing time will reduce the noise level and enable substantially tighter constraints on the EoR signal.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a method to estimate the 21 cm bispectrum from MWA observations at z=8.2 using Smooth Component Filtering for foreground mitigation, validates the pipeline with simulations, applies it to real data, and places constraints on EoR brightness temperature fluctuations.
AI.motivation: The 21 cm bispectrum is a powerful probe of the Epoch of Reionization but is severely hindered by dominant astrophysical foregrounds that must be mitigated to access the cosmological signal.
AI.method: Uses Smooth Component Filtering (SCF) to mitigate foregrounds in Murchison Widefield Array observations at 154.2 MHz (z=8.2), validates the pipeline with simulated 21 cm signals, estimates the cylindrical bispectrum, and evaluates the 3D spherical bispectrum in specific k-space regions.
AI.result: SCF achieves 3-4 orders of magnitude foreground suppression in the cylindrical bispectrum amplitude, cleans the EoR window at small k_perp, and places constraints on mean cube brightness temperature fluctuations: lower limit Δ³_LL = -(1.25×10⁴)³ mK³ and upper limit Δ³_UL = (1.22×10⁴)³ mK³ at k₁=0.281 Mpc⁻¹, consistent with system noise fluctuations.
AI.conclusion: The pipeline successfully mitigates foregrounds and enables bispectrum estimation from MWA data, with current limits consistent with noise; additional observing time will reduce noise and provide tighter constraints on the EoR signal.

title: ELVES-Field: Isolated Dwarf Galaxy Quenched Fractions Rise Below $M_* \approx 10^7$ $M_\odot$
summary: We use a new sample of low-mass ($M_* < 10^9$ $M_\odot$) isolated galaxies from the Exploration of Local VolumE Survey - Field (ELVES-Field) to examine the star formation properties and sizes of field dwarf galaxies in the Local Volume (LV; $D<10$ Mpc). This volume-limited sample was selected from nearly 3,000 square degrees of imaging, relying on surface brightness fluctuations to determine distances to the majority of the systems and is complete to $M_* \approx 10^6$ $M_\odot$. Across the surveyed area, we catalog over 2300 candidate LV dwarfs, of which we confirm 95 as genuine LV members and reject over 1600 as background contaminants, with the remaining 600 candidates still requiring a distance measurement. Of the confirmed LV dwarfs, 46 are either new discoveries or confirmed via a distance measurement for the first time here. We explore different environmental criteria to select isolated dwarfs but primarily focus on dwarfs that are $>2\times R_{\mathrm{vir}}$ in projection from any known group with $M_\star > 10^9$ $M_\odot$. We find that, at higher dwarf masses ($M_\star \gtrsim 10^7$ $M_\odot$), essentially all field dwarfs are star-forming as has been found before. In contrast, at $M_\star \lesssim 10^7$ $M_\odot$, $\sim30\%$ of field dwarfs appear to be quenched. Finally, we find that isolated dwarfs are noticeably smaller ($\sim 20\%$) than satellite dwarfs of the same stellar mass, regardless of quenched status.

AI.tldr: Analysis of low-mass isolated dwarf galaxies in the Local Volume reveals that while higher-mass field dwarfs are all star-forming, about 30% of lower-mass field dwarfs are quenched, and isolated dwarfs are ~20% smaller than satellite dwarfs of the same stellar mass.
AI.motivation: To examine the star formation properties and sizes of field dwarf galaxies in the Local Volume using a new sample of low-mass isolated galaxies, addressing how isolation affects dwarf galaxy evolution compared to satellite systems.
AI.method: Used a volume-limited sample from ELVES-Field survey covering nearly 3,000 square degrees, employing surface brightness fluctuations for distance measurements. Selected isolated dwarfs based on environmental criteria (primarily >2× R_vir from any known group with M_* > 10^9 M_⊙). Cataloged over 2300 candidate LV dwarfs, confirmed 95 as genuine members, rejected over 1600 as background contaminants.
AI.result: At higher dwarf masses (M_* ≳ 10^7 M_⊙), essentially all field dwarfs are star-forming. At lower masses (M_* ≲ 10^7 M_⊙), ~30% of field dwarfs appear to be quenched. Isolated dwarfs are noticeably smaller (~20%) than satellite dwarfs of the same stellar mass, regardless of quenched status.
AI.conclusion: Isolation significantly affects dwarf galaxy properties: field dwarfs show different star formation quenching patterns than satellite systems, with a substantial fraction of low-mass field dwarfs being quenched despite their isolation, and isolated dwarfs are systematically smaller than their satellite counterparts.

title: Cosmic voids evolution in modified gravity via hydrodynamics
summary: We present a hydrodynamical description of spherical void evolution in modified gravity (MG), extending the standard General Relativity (GR) and dynamical dark energy treatment by encoding gravity modifications into effective couplings that enter the Euler and Poisson equations. This yields a compact non-linear evolution equation for the Eulerian density contrast, controlled by a time- and density-dependent effective gravitational strength, and provides a direct map between model functions and void observables. We apply the framework to the luminal Galileon class of models, where derivative self-interactions generate Vainshtein screening and might lead to a breakdown of the physical branch in sufficiently underdense regions. Exploiting this feature, we apply the void-informed viability requirement that translates into bounds on the theory parameter space and, equivalently, on the minimum attainable void depth as a function of redshift. For viable parameters of a concrete model, we quantify the impact of MG on isolated void evolution, the Lagrangian to Eulerian mapping, and the shell-crossing threshold. Relative to GR, we find a clear hierarchy of MG effects, with ${\cal O}(10\%)$ modifications in the gravitational couplings, percent-level shifts in the void density evolution, and sub-percent deviations in both the mapping and the shell-crossing thresholds. Moreover, within the adopted parametrization, we show analytically that voids always lie in an unscreened regime on the physical branch. Overall, the formalism provides a self-consistent route to predict void dynamics and consistency constraints in a broad class of MG models.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a hydrodynamical framework for spherical void evolution in modified gravity, applies it to luminal Galileon models, and uses void observables to constrain theory parameters.
AI.motivation: To extend the description of spherical void evolution from General Relativity to modified gravity theories, providing a direct connection between model functions and void observables for testing gravity modifications.
AI.method: Develops a hydrodynamical description encoding gravity modifications into effective couplings in Euler and Poisson equations, yielding a non-linear evolution equation for Eulerian density contrast with time- and density-dependent effective gravitational strength.
AI.result: For luminal Galileon models, finds clear hierarchy of MG effects: O(10%) modifications in gravitational couplings, percent-level shifts in void density evolution, and sub-percent deviations in Lagrangian-Eulerian mapping and shell-crossing thresholds. Shows voids always lie in unscreened regime on physical branch.
AI.conclusion: The formalism provides a self-consistent route to predict void dynamics and derive consistency constraints for a broad class of modified gravity models using void observables.

title: Varstrometry for Off-nucleus and Dual Subkiloparsec AGN (VODKA): Three Quadruply Lensed Quasars at Cosmic Noon in HST and JWST
summary: We present results from imaging observations of three quadruply lensed quasars by Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) at redshifts $z = 2.550$, 2.975, and 1.500. We model our targets assuming a singular isothermal ellipsoid mass profile and an elliptical SÃ\c{opyright}rsic profile for the lensing galaxies, and reconstruct the geometric configuration of each system with measured Einstein radii of 0.44$'$, 0.58$'$, and 0.49$'$. While no spectroscopic measurements are available for the lenses, we constrain the redshift of each lens to $0.5 < z < 1.2$, $1.0 < z < 1.5$, and $0.4 < z < 0.9$. For all three lenses, the best-fit light model yield a typical de Vaucouleurs $n_{\rm S\acute{e}rsic} \sim 4$ profile and an effective radius $R_e$ around $\sim 1.5 - 3.5$ kpc. We accordingly classify the three lenses as early-type galaxies at an intermediate to high redshift, a common type for strong lensing galaxies. Compared to other known quadruple lenses, the lensing galaxies in this work are at the lower end of the distribution of Einstein radii and upper end of the distribution of the lens redshifts. They represent an interesting quadrant of subarcsecond-separation lenses in the population of single-galaxy strong lensing which have been largely unexplored yet and will be great targets of interest in upcoming high-resolution lensing surveys.

AI.tldr: HST and JWST observations of three quadruply lensed quasars reveal early-type lensing galaxies with small Einstein radii (0.44-0.58") and intermediate-to-high redshifts, representing an underexplored population of subarcsecond-separation strong lenses.
AI.motivation: To characterize an underexplored population of strong gravitational lenses with subarcsecond separations and constrain properties of lensing galaxies at intermediate-to-high redshifts.
AI.method: Used HST and JWST imaging observations of three quadruply lensed quasars. Modeled lensing galaxies with singular isothermal ellipsoid mass profiles and elliptical Sérsic light profiles. Reconstructed geometric configurations and measured Einstein radii, Sérsic indices, and effective radii.
AI.result: Measured Einstein radii of 0.44", 0.58", and 0.49". Constrained lens redshifts to 0.5<z<1.2, 1.0<z<1.5, and 0.4<z<0.9. Best-fit models show de Vaucouleurs profiles (n~4) with effective radii ~1.5-3.5 kpc. Identified lenses as early-type galaxies at lower end of Einstein radius distribution and upper end of redshift distribution among known quadruple lenses.
AI.conclusion: These systems represent an interesting, largely unexplored quadrant of subarcsecond-separation strong lenses with small Einstein radii and intermediate-to-high redshifts, making them valuable targets for future high-resolution lensing surveys.

title: PRODIGE - envelope to disk with NOEMA: VII. (Complex) organic molecules in the NGC1333 IRAS4B1 outflow: A new laboratory for shock chemistry
summary: Shock chemistry is an excellent tool to shed light on the formation and destruction mechanisms of complex organic molecules (COMs). The L1157-mm outflow is the only low-mass protostellar outflow that has extensively been studied in this regard. Using the data taken as part of the PRODIGE (PROtostars & DIsks: Global Evolution) large program, we aim to map COM emission and derive the molecular composition of the protostellar outflow driven by the Class 0 protostar NGC1333 IRAS4B1 to introduce it as a new laboratory to study the impact of shocks on COM chemistry. In addition to typical outflow tracers such as SiO and CO, outflow emission is seen from H2CO, HNCO, and HC3N, as well as from the COMs CH3OH, CH3CN, and CH3CHO, and even from deuterated species such as DCN, D2CO, and CH2DOH. Maps of integrated intensity ratios between CH3OH and DCN, D2CO, and CH3CHO reveal gradients with distance from the protostar. Intensity ratio maps of HC3N and CH3CN with respect to CH3OH peak in the southern lobe where temperatures are highest. Rotational temperatures derived towards two positions, one in each lobe, are found in the range ~50-100 K. Abundances with respect to CH3OH are higher by factors of a few than for the L1157-B1. In conclusion, for the first time, we securely detected the COMs CH3CN, CH3CHO, and CH2DOH in the IRAS 4B1 outflow, serendipitously with limited sensitivity and bandwidth. Targeted observations will enable the discovery of new COMs and a more detailed analysis of their emission. Morphological differences between molecules in the IRAS 4B1 outflow lobes and their relative abundances provide first proof that this outflow is a promising new laboratory for shock chemistry, which will offer crucial information on COM formation and destruction as well as outflow structure and kinematics.

AI.tldr: First detection of complex organic molecules (CH3CN, CH3CHO, CH2DOH) in IRAS 4B1 protostellar outflow reveals it as a promising new laboratory for studying shock chemistry and COM formation/destruction mechanisms.
AI.motivation: To map COM emission and characterize the molecular composition of the NGC1333 IRAS4B1 protostellar outflow, establishing it as a new laboratory for studying shock chemistry effects on complex organic molecule formation and destruction.
AI.method: Used PRODIGE large program data to map molecular emission, analyze integrated intensity ratios between species (CH3OH vs DCN, D2CO, CH3CHO), derive rotational temperatures (~50-100 K), and compare abundances with the well-studied L1157-B1 outflow.
AI.result: First secure detection of COMs CH3CN, CH3CHO, and CH2DOH in IRAS 4B1 outflow; identified spatial gradients in molecular ratios; found higher COM abundances (by factors of few) compared to L1157-B1; temperature-dependent intensity ratios observed in southern lobe.
AI.conclusion: IRAS 4B1 outflow is a promising new laboratory for shock chemistry studies, offering crucial insights into COM formation/destruction mechanisms and outflow structure/kinematics, with targeted observations needed for more detailed analysis and discovery of additional COMs.

title: MIDIS: The identification of deep MIRI-red sources as candidates for extreme Balmer-break and line emitting galaxies at high-z
summary: We investigate the detection and nature of 5.6~μm MIRI-red sources in the MIRI Deep Imaging Survey (MIDIS), covering 2.4~arcmin$^2$ in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. MIDIS is the deepest JWST/MIRI survey to date, probing faint limits and enabling studies of rare high-redshift galaxy populations. We define MIRI-red sources as those detected at 5$σ$ significance in MIRI/F560W with red colors: $m_{\rm F444W} - m_{\rm F560W} \ge 0.5$. Using an empirical methodology, we estimate the purity and completeness of MIRI detections and find that a 5-sigma detection at 28.75 mag has a purity of 92\% and completeness of 54\%. We identify seven MIRI-red galaxy candidates, including an F115W dropout consistent with a high-redshift galaxy candidate. We explore possible physical origins for the MIRI-red population, including active galactic nuclei, dust-obscured galaxies, extreme emission-line galaxies, evolved stellar populations, and Little Red Dots (LRDs). Given the proximity of the F444W and F560W filters and the depth of MIDIS, MIRI-red galaxies are consistent with emission-line galaxies with $EW_0(Hα) \ge 750$ Å or $EW_0(Hβ+ [OIII]) \ge 600$ Å, or high-redshift Balmer breaks of at least 1.6. We also discuss an extreme MIRI-red galaxy undetected in F444W, a potential MIRI-only source, for which we derive $EW_0(Hα) \sim 6000$ Å and $EW_0(Hβ+ [OIII]) \sim 4000$ Å, or high-$z$ LRD analogs with Balmer breaks of 6.3. Finally, we find fewer MIRI-red detections than expected from extrapolations of the H$α$ or H$β$+[OIII] line luminosity functions, consistent with previous deep searches, while the absence of $z>10$ LRD candidates agrees with theoretical expectations for the MIDIS volume.

AI.tldr: MIDIS survey identifies rare MIRI-red galaxies in HUDF using JWST/MIRI, finding 7 candidates including extreme emission-line galaxies and potential high-z sources, with detection rates lower than expected from line luminosity functions.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature and properties of rare MIRI-red sources in the deepest JWST/MIRI survey to date, probing faint limits and enabling studies of high-redshift galaxy populations that are otherwise difficult to detect.
AI.method: Used MIDIS (MIRI Deep Imaging Survey) covering 2.4 arcmin² in HUDF, defined MIRI-red sources as 5σ detections in MIRI/F560W with red colors (m_F444W - m_F560W ≥ 0.5), applied empirical methodology to estimate purity/completeness, and explored physical origins through emission-line equivalent widths and Balmer breaks.
AI.result: Found 7 MIRI-red galaxy candidates with 92% purity and 54% completeness at 28.75 mag; identified extreme emission-line galaxies with EW₀(Hα) ≥ 750 Å or EW₀(Hβ+[OIII]) ≥ 600 Å, and one extreme MIRI-red galaxy undetected in F444W with EW₀(Hα) ∼ 6000 Å; detection rates lower than expected from line luminosity function extrapolations.
AI.conclusion: MIRI-red sources in MIDIS represent rare populations including extreme emission-line galaxies and potential high-redshift candidates; the lower-than-expected detection rates and absence of z>10 LRD candidates align with theoretical expectations for the survey volume, providing constraints on these rare galaxy populations.

title: Dynamical Modelling of Galactic Kinematics using Neural Networks
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures. Preprint of conference proceedings to appear in Machine Learning for Astrophysics 2024, Springer Nature (eds. F. Bufano, E. Sciacca & S. Riggi)
summary: The advent of integral field data has revolutionised the study of galaxy evolution. A key component of this is dynamical modelling methods which have allowed for crucial insights to be made from kinematic data. Despite this importance, most dynamical models make a number of key assumptions which do not hold for real galaxies. These include assumptions about the geometry (axisymmetry or triaxiality), the shape of the velocity ellipsoid, and the shape of the underlying stellar distribution. At the same time, machine learning methods are becoming increasingly powerful, with many applications appearing in astronomy. As a first step towards building new dynamical modelling methods with machine learning, it is important to understand the types of machine learning architectures that are best fit for dynamical modelling. To investigate this, we construct a training set of dynamical models of early-type galaxies using Jeans Anisotropic Modelling (JAM). We then train a neural network on this data using the parameters of JAM and mock photometry as the input. We are able to accurately model JAM galaxies with relatively simple machine learning architectures, leading to a significant speed increase over traditional JAM modelling.

AI.tldr: Neural networks can accurately and rapidly model galaxy dynamics using JAM parameters and mock photometry, offering significant speed improvements over traditional methods.
AI.motivation: Current dynamical modeling methods for galaxies rely on unrealistic assumptions about geometry, velocity ellipsoid shape, and stellar distribution. Machine learning offers potential for more flexible and efficient modeling approaches.
AI.method: Constructed training set of dynamical models for early-type galaxies using Jeans Anisotropic Modelling (JAM). Trained neural networks using JAM parameters and mock photometry as inputs to learn the dynamical modeling process.
AI.result: Neural networks can accurately model JAM galaxies with relatively simple architectures, achieving significant speed increases compared to traditional JAM modeling approaches.
AI.conclusion: Machine learning architectures show promise for dynamical modeling of galaxies, offering faster and potentially more flexible alternatives to traditional methods with restrictive assumptions.

title: Interstellar Formation of Thioethanal (CH$_{3}$CHS). Gas-Phase and Ice-Surface Mechanisms involving Secondary Sulfur Products
summary: The formation pathways of sulfur-bearing species in the interstellar medium are crucial to understand astrochemical processes in cold molecular clouds and to gain new insights about the sulfur budget in these regions. We aim to explore the recently detected, thioethanal (CH$_{3}$CHS) formation mechanisms from thioethanol (CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$SH) as a precursor in addition to secondary sulfur products. The electronic structure methods and density functional theory for both gas-phase and ice-grain surface environments is employed. To mimic interstellar ice-mantles, we use medium (W6) and large amorphized (W22) water clusters as implemented in Binding Energy Evaluation protocol. A barrierless formation mechanism for CH$_{3}$CHS under low-temperature interstellar conditions is identified, in the gas phase. Surface environments modulate activation barriers in a site-specific manner, elucidated through both Langmuir-Hinshelwood and Eley-Rideal initiated surface reaction pathways. Compared to oxygen analogs, sulfur chemistry enables alternate pathways due to weaker S-H bonding, with a competing route forming ethane-1,1-di-thiol (CH$_{3}$CH(SH)SH), on the ice-grain surface, potentially reducing CH$_{3}$CHS yields. The first accurate binding energy for thioethanol on water ice is also reported, confirming its greater volatility than ethanol. The proposed mechanism offers a tentative hypothesis for the apparent mutual exclusive detections of the CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$SH and CH$_{3}$CHS in TMC-1, Orion, and Sgr B2(N), that further requires validation through quantitative astrochemical modeling and also to distinguish this chemical differentiation from observational sensitivity limitations. These qualitative findings highlight the multifaceted chemical behavior of sulfur-bearing organics in the interstellar medium and support CH$_{3}$CH(SH)SH as promising astro-chemical targets.

AI.tldr: Study explores formation mechanisms of thioethanal (CH₃CHS) from thioethanol (CH₃CH₂SH) in interstellar environments, identifying barrierless gas-phase pathways and surface-modulated reactions on ice grains.
AI.motivation: To understand sulfur-bearing species formation pathways in cold molecular clouds and address the sulfur budget problem, particularly explaining the apparent mutual exclusive detections of thioethanol and thioethanal in interstellar regions like TMC-1, Orion, and Sgr B2(N).
AI.method: Employed electronic structure methods and density functional theory for gas-phase and ice-grain surface environments. Used medium (W6) and large amorphized (W22) water clusters to mimic interstellar ice-mantles via Binding Energy Evaluation protocol. Analyzed both Langmuir-Hinshelwood and Eley-Rideal surface reaction pathways.
AI.result: Identified barrierless formation mechanism for CH₃CHS in gas phase under low-temperature conditions. Surface environments modulate activation barriers site-specifically. Sulfur chemistry enables alternate pathways due to weaker S-H bonding, with competing route forming ethane-1,1-di-thiol (CH₃CH(SH)SH) on ice surfaces, potentially reducing CH₃CHS yields. Reported first accurate binding energy for thioethanol on water ice, confirming its greater volatility than ethanol.
AI.conclusion: Proposed mechanism offers tentative hypothesis for mutual exclusive detections of CH₃CH₂SH and CH₃CHS in interstellar regions, requiring validation through quantitative astrochemical modeling. Findings highlight multifaceted chemical behavior of sulfur-bearing organics and support CH₃CH(SH)SH as promising astrochemical target.

title: MUSEQuBES: Probing Anisotropies in Gas and Metal Distributions in the Circumgalactic Medium
comment: Submitted to ApJ. Comments are welcome
summary: We investigate the azimuthal dependence of H I and O VI-bearing gas in the circumgalactic medium (CGM) of 113 isolated galaxies in the redshift range 0.12 < z < 0.75, including 91 new measurements from the MUSE Quasar-fields Blind Emitters Survey (MUSEQuBES). The H I covering fraction (k_HI) within the virial radius (Rvir) of low-mass (7 < log10(M*/Msun)< 9) galaxies, for a threshold column density of log10(N(HI)/cm^-2) = 14.5, exhibits an enhancement along both the disk plane (azimuthal angle phi < 20 degree) and in the polar direction (phi > 70 degree). In contrast, such a bimodal distribution is not observed for higher mass galaxies (9 < log10(M*/Msun) < 11.3). Similarly, the O VI covering fraction (k_OVI), for a threshold of log10(N(OVI)/cm^-2) = 14.0, shows a tentative enhancement along both the projected major and minor axes for low-mass galaxies. In contrast, O VI-bearing gas around higher- mass galaxies appears more uniformly distributed, with no significant azimuthal dependence. Finally, using the halo circular-velocity-normalized pixel-velocity two-point correlation function (TPCF), we find that O VI absorbers are kinematically narrower along the disk plane compared to the polar directions of the host galaxies with similar stellar mass distributions. The observed isotropic distribution of O VI in high-mass halos suggests that its spatial distribution is governed by global halo properties; however, the O VI kinematics retain memory of the site of origin.

AI.tldr: Study of 113 isolated galaxies reveals azimuthal dependence of H I and O VI gas in low-mass galaxies' CGM, showing bimodal distribution along disk plane and polar directions, while high-mass galaxies show uniform distribution.
AI.motivation: To investigate the azimuthal dependence and spatial distribution of H I and O VI-bearing gas in the circumgalactic medium of isolated galaxies, and understand how these distributions vary with galaxy mass.
AI.method: Analysis of 113 isolated galaxies (0.12 < z < 0.75) including 91 new measurements from MUSEQuBES survey, examining H I and O VI covering fractions within virial radius, and using halo circular-velocity-normalized pixel-velocity two-point correlation function to study kinematics.
AI.result: Low-mass galaxies show bimodal H I distribution with enhancement along disk plane (φ < 20°) and polar direction (φ > 70°), while high-mass galaxies show uniform distribution. O VI shows similar pattern with tentative enhancement along major/minor axes for low-mass galaxies. O VI absorbers are kinematically narrower along disk plane compared to polar directions.
AI.conclusion: The isotropic O VI distribution in high-mass halos suggests global halo properties govern spatial distribution, while O VI kinematics retain memory of origin site, indicating different physical processes shaping CGM in low vs. high-mass galaxies.

title: A Chemodynamical Census of the Milky Way's Ultra-Faint Compact Satellites. I. A First Population-Level Look at the Internal Kinematics and Metallicities of 19 Extremely-Low-Mass Halo Stellar Systems
comment: 63 pages (main) + 18 pages (references + appendix), 30 Figures, 6 Tables. Will submit to ApJ in one week; comments welcome. Brief summary available here: https://wcerny.github.io/compactsatellites/. Repository with spectroscopic member catalogs: https://zenodo.org/records/18612486. Forthcoming Paper II will explore the orbits, accretion histories, and tidal influences of the same sample
summary: Deep, wide-area photometric surveys have uncovered a population of compact ($r_{1/2} \approx$ 1-15 pc), extremely-low-mass ($M_* \approx$ 20-4000 $M_{\odot}$) stellar systems in the Milky Way halo that are smaller in size than known ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs) and substantially fainter than most classical globular clusters (GCs). Very little is known about the nature and origins of this population of "Ultra-Faint Compact Satellites" (UFCSs) owing to a dearth of spectroscopic measurements. Here, we present the first spectroscopic census of these compact systems based on Magellan/IMACS and Keck/DEIMOS observations of 19 individual UFCSs, representing $\sim$2/3 of the known population. We securely measure mean radial velocities for all 19 systems, velocity dispersions for 15 (predominantly upper limits), metallicities for 17, metallicity dispersions for 8, and $\textit{Gaia}$-based mean proper motions for 18. This large new spectroscopic sample provides the first insights into population-level trends for these extreme satellites. We demonstrate that: (1) the UFCSs are kinematically colder, on average, than the UFDs, disfavoring very dense dark matter halos in most cases, (2) the UFCS population is chemically diverse, spanning a factor of $\sim$300 in mean iron abundance ($\rm -3.3 \lesssim [Fe/H] \lesssim -0.8$), with multiple systems falling beneath the "metallicity floor" proposed for GCs, and (3) while some higher-metallicity and/or younger UFCSs are clearly star clusters, the dynamical and/or chemical evidence allows the possibility that up to $\sim$50% of the UFCSs in our sample (9 of 19) may represent the smallest and least-massive galaxies yet discovered.

AI.tldr: First spectroscopic study of 19 Ultra-Faint Compact Satellites (UFCSs) reveals they are kinematically colder than ultra-faint dwarfs, chemically diverse, and up to 50% may be the smallest galaxies ever discovered.
AI.motivation: UFCSs are compact, extremely-low-mass stellar systems discovered in Milky Way halo surveys, but their nature and origins remain poorly understood due to lack of spectroscopic measurements.
AI.method: Magellan/IMACS and Keck/DEIMOS spectroscopic observations of 19 UFCSs (~2/3 of known population), measuring radial velocities, velocity dispersions, metallicities, metallicity dispersions, and Gaia-based proper motions.
AI.result: UFCSs are kinematically colder than UFDs (disfavoring dense dark matter halos), chemically diverse (spanning ~300x in iron abundance, some below GC metallicity floor), and up to 9 of 19 may be smallest galaxies discovered.
AI.conclusion: First spectroscopic census reveals UFCSs as a distinct population with diverse origins - some are star clusters, but up to 50% may represent the smallest and least-massive galaxies yet discovered.
